newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds capped at 100.40, U.S. data could cause fall.
newsitem.headline: Bunds capped at 100.40, U.S. data could cause fall.

text.p: German Bunds firmed in early trade on Friday but the gains were expected to be limited ahead of the release of key U.S. data due later in the day.

Dealers said Bunds may slide after the release of U.S. March retail sales which are expected to show a 0.6 percent rise according to a consensus forecast by economists polled by Reuters -- a sign of robust economic growth which could fuel fears of another U.S. credit tightening.
The scope for Bunds to outperform Treasuries was limited given that the spread of 10-year Treasuries over Bunds, at 112 basis points at 0708 GMT, was close to record highs.
"With the spread as big as it is a further decoupling from the U.S. is difficult," said Helmut Kaiser, bond analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Frankfurt.

Bunds have outperformed Treasuries because Germany and the U.S. are at different stages of their economic cycles, with German economic growth and inflation still weak enough to make an interest rate rise here unlikely anytime soon.
But dealers said the steepness of the German yield curve, which was supporting Bunds, and the prospect of continued weak inflation had now largely been priced in.
U.S. March producer prices are also due at 1230 GMT but analysts said retail sales were the more important number since it indicated the pace of economic growth.
June Bund futures were trading at 100.22 at 0800 GMT, up 11 basis points from Thursday's close, after rising as high as 100.29 earlier in the session.
Dealers saw Bunds capped at 100.40 ahead of the data.
Kaiser at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said he saw a risk of Bunds falling below 100 if retail sales were up 0.6 percent.
One dealer said losses could accelerate if futures fall below technical support at 99.80.
